correction: If using the revised comparable annual CPI series,the2022rate is6.9%,not7.9%;2023is5.9%. The7.9%value was genuinely published17January2023on the old2015base and was revised22February2023. The very original release linked in submissionfootnote10now carries an explicit revision warning. Footnote11links theJanuary2024release that alreadystates6.9%for2022.
effect: On a current comparable-series reading,the passage overstates the2022inflation benchmark by1percentagepoint and makes its crisis-pressure example stronger. Both6.9%and5.9%remain well above the draft’s3.5%threshold.
limits: The7.9%number is not fabricated: it belongs to an authentic earlier statistical vintage. Already implemented contractual index adjustments may remain legally effective after statistical rebasing; this investigation does not recalculate anyone’s rent. Annual-average inflation is not itself the increase applicable to every individual tenancy. The submission does not explicitly name a base year,so the possibility that it deliberately refers to the original historical rate must be considered. No intent is inferred.
context_and_alternatives: Full20-page submission read; claimphysical11and requestphysical13. Correctly addresses the original3.5%consultation cap,not the later government formula.

Historical-vintage alternative is plausible because the author links the originalJanuary2023release directly. direction_explanation: If the unqualified historical rate is treated as erroneous current-series presentation,the higher2022rate strengthens the described inflation shock supporting stricter rent caps. This conditional direction is separate from whether an error has been established.
